| Item | Status | Notes |

## 2. Section 1 — Official documentation and repository

### 2.1 Official GitHub repository

- `https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/docs/LightRAG-API-Server.md` [call-09f68176] [call-918fd425] [call-78935ce9] [call-3002da7b] [call-2c556838] [call-c2b256ee]

However, there is **no independent authoritative confirmation** in the boundary (e.g., a PyPI project page, a separate project website, or an official announcement) beyond the repository itself.

---

## 3. Section 2 — Supported storage backends

LightRAG requires four storage types: **KVStorage** (caching LLM responses and text chunks), **VectorStorage** (embedding vectors), **GraphStorage** (entity–relation graphs), and **DocStatusStorage** (document indexing status) [call-78935ce9; https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/docs/ProgramingWithCore.md]. The default stores are in-memory databases with local file persistence, suitable only for small-scale testing/evaluation, not production [call-c21ffffd] [call-7876a2cc].

### 3.1 Key-value storage backends
**Partially supported.** Options named in the boundary:
- `JsonKVStorage` (default) [call-35215f23 observation via dev.to]
- `RedisKVStorage` [call-38fa5da4; https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/docs/ProgramingWithCore.md]
- `PGKVStorage` [call-38fa5da4] [call-3002da7b] [call-dfa96a6f]
- `MongoKVStorage` [call-38fa5da4] [call-dfa96a6f]

PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and OpenSearch are also described as single-backend options able to cover KV among other roles [call-35215f23 observation] [call-7876a2cc].

### 3.2 Vector storage backends
**Partially supported.** Options named:
- `MilvusVectorDBStorage` [call-38fa5da4] [call-31224b71] [call-7876a2cc]
- `QdrantVectorDBStorage` [call-38fa5da4] [call-7876a2cc]
- `FaissVectorDBStorage` [call-38fa5da4] [call-31224b71]
- `NanoVectorDBStorage` [call-38fa5da4] (default vector store per dev.to observation)
- `PGVectorStorage` [call-38fa5da4] [call-3002da7b]
- `MongoDB` / `MongoVectorDBStorage` [call-38fa5da4] [call-dfa96a6f]
- `Chroma` appears only in the Medium summary [call-31224b71] and is **not** in the call-38fa5da4 list that references the official docs — treated as an omission/conflict, not confirmed.

### 3.3 Graph storage backends
**Partially supported.** Options named:
- `Neo4JStorage` [call-38fa5da4] [call-b75d434f] [call-7876a2cc] [call-31224b71]
- `MemgraphStorage` [call-38fa5da4] [call-7876a2cc]
- `NetworkXStorage` [call-38fa5da4]
- `OpenSearchGraphStorage` [call-38fa5da4]
- `PGGraphStorage` [call-3002da7b] [call-f64c3f09] [call-b75d434f] (requires PostgreSQL + Apache AGE)

### 3.4 Document status storage options
**Partially supported.** Options named:
- `JsonDocStatusStorage` (default) [call-38fa5da4 — excerpt truncated] [call-35215f23 observation]
- `PGDocStatusStorage` [call-3002da7b] [call-b75d434f]
- `MongoDocStatusStorage` [call-dfa96a6f]
- `RedisDocStatusStorage` [call-35215f23 observation via dev.to]

### 3.5 Backend summary table

| Storage type | Production-capable options named in boundary | Default (testing only) |
|---|---|---|
| Key-value | PGKVStorage, RedisKVStorage, MongoKVStorage; PostgreSQL/MongoDB/OpenSearch as single-backend | JsonKVStorage |
| Vector | PGVectorStorage, MilvusVectorDBStorage, QdrantVectorDBStorage, FaissVectorDBStorage, NanoVectorDBStorage, MongoDB | NanoVectorDBStorage |
| Graph | PGGraphStorage (PostgreSQL + Apache AGE), Neo4JStorage, MemgraphStorage, NetworkXStorage, OpenSearchGraphStorage | NetworkXStorage |
| Doc status | PGDocStatusStorage, MongoDocStatusStorage, RedisDocStatusStorage | JsonDocStatusStorage |

**Official production guidance:** PostgreSQL is recommended for production because it can serve **all four** storage types on its own (`PGKVStorage`, `PGVectorStorage`, `PGGraphStorage`, `PGDocStatusStorage`) [call-918fd425] [call-78935ce9] [call-c21ffffd] [call-7876a2cc]. MongoDB and OpenSearch are the other single-backend production options; Milvus/Qdrant (vector) and Neo4j/Memgraph (graph) are specialized alternatives [call-c21ffffd] [call-7876a2cc] [call-31224b71].

---

## 4. Section 3 — Differences between available storage options

The boundary provides **directional** differences but not a full comparative matrix.

| Dimension | What the boundary states | Sources |
|---|---|---|
| KV role | Caches LLM responses and text chunks | [call-78935ce9] |
| KV options | JSON / PostgreSQL / Redis named for KV | [call-31224b71] |
| Vector role | Embedding vectors | [call-78935ce9] |
| Vector options | FAISS, Chroma, Milvus named; PG vector supports HNSW and IVFFlat indexes (`POSTGRES_VECTOR_INDEX_TYPE`, `POSTGRES_HNSW_M`, `POSTGRES_HNSW_EF`, `POSTGRES_IVFFLAT_LISTS`) | [call-31224b71] [call-2c556838] |
| Graph role | Entity–relation graphs | [call-78935ce9] |
| Graph options | Neo4j and PostgreSQL AGE named; Apache AGE is **required** for `PGGraphStorage` — a stock PostgreSQL image cannot provide it; AGE supports openCypher | [call-31224b71] [call-69bb6213] [call-f64c3f09] |
| Doc-status role | Document indexing status | [call-78935ce9] |
| Production suitability | Default in-memory + local file persistence = small-scale testing only; PostgreSQL recommended for production; specialized DBs (Milvus/Qdrant vector, Neo4j/Memgraph graph) for workloads needing them | [call-7876a2cc] [call-c21ffffd] [call-31224b71] |

**Conflicts/omissions:** Chroma appears as a vector option in one summary [call-31224b71] but is absent from the list tied to the official docs [call-38fa5da4]. No per-backend trade-off detail (e.g., Neo4j vs Memgraph vs NetworkX) is provided.

---

## 5. Section 4 — PostgreSQL / Neon suitability

### 5.1 PostgreSQL support status
**Supported.** PostgreSQL is an officially recommended production backend serving all four storage roles [call-69bb6213] [call-f64c3f09] [call-3002da7b] [call-c21ffffd]. For graph storage it uses `PGGraphStorage`, which requires **pgvector + Apache AGE**; the official Docker image referenced is `gzdaniel/postgres-for-rag:pg18-age-pgvector` (bundles Apache AGE and pgvector), and `pgvector/pgvector:pg18` is suggested for non-graph storage [call-f64c3f09; https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/docs/DockerDeployment.md]. A Railway production template uses PostgreSQL for all four storage roles and is described as production-grade [call-69bb6213; https://railway.com/deploy/lightrag-knowledge-graph-rag-postgres-production--lightrag-postgres-graph-rag].

### 5.2 Neon compatibility
**Partially supported — compatibility not confirmed.**
- Neon is a serverless PostgreSQL provider; the boundary confirms Neon supports PostgreSQL and extensions such as `pg_embedding` for vector search [call-3138b8ec] [call-209c58b4] [call-cc7fef0c; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/postgresql/azure-ai/generative-ai-age-overview].
- **Apache AGE support on Neon is not confirmed.** Three sources state Neon does **not explicitly mention** Apache AGE and that it is unknown whether Neon serverless PostgreSQL supports AGE [call-3138b8ec] [call-209c58b4] [call-cc7fef0c]. One source states Neon supports extensions "including Apache AGE" but then concedes there is no specific LightRAG-on-serverless information [call-9c56041b].
- Because `PGGraphStorage` depends on Apache AGE, **Neon cannot be confirmed as a drop-in replacement for the full four-role PostgreSQL setup** unless AGE availability on Neon is verified.

### 5.3 Production suitability evaluation
**Partially supported.** Self-hosted or managed PostgreSQL with pgvector + Apache AGE is supported for production (Railway template, official Docker image) [call-69bb6213] [call-f64c3f09]. Neon serverless suitability is **uncertain** due to the unconfirmed AGE dependency for graph storage.

---

## 6. Section 5 — Compatibility limitations and configuration considerations

### 6.1 Compatibility limitations
**Partially supported (not exhaustive).**
- **Stock PostgreSQL is insufficient for graph storage:** Apache AGE extension is required; a stock PostgreSQL image cannot provide `PGGraphStorage` [call-69bb6213] [call-f64c3f09].
- **Mixed-stack issue:** GitHub issue #860 reports that using Milvus + Neo4j + PostgreSQL together leaves the `lightrag_doc_chunks` table empty after document processing [call-b75d434f; https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/issues/860].
- **MongoDB vector storage:** reported as available only on MongoDB Atlas Cloud [call-35215f23 observation via dev.to].
- The boundary explicitly states there is **no definitive answer on the compatibility limitations of all mentioned storage backends** [call-c21ffffd].

### 6.2 Configuration requirements
**Supported.** Environment variables for PostgreSQL storage selection:
- `LIGHTRAG_KV_STORAGE=PGKVStorage`
- `LIGHTRAG_VECTOR_STORAGE=PGVectorStorage`
- `LIGHTRAG_GRAPH_STORAGE=PGGraphStorage`
- `LIGHTRAG_DOC_STATUS_STORAGE=PGDocStatusStorage`
- PostgreSQL connection: `POSTGRES_USER`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `POSTGRES_DATABASE`, `POSTGRES_HOST`, `POSTGRES_PORT`; additional `PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT`, `PGCLIENTENCODING`, `PGTARGE...` (truncated) [call-3002da7b; https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/docs/LightRAG-API-Server.md].

Neon/PostgreSQL-specific additions reported:
- `POSTGRES_MAX_CONNECTIONS`, `POSTGRES_VECTOR_INDEX_TYPE`, `POSTGRES_HNSW_M`, `POSTGRES_HNSW_EF`, `POSTGRES_IVFFLAT_LISTS`; vector index types HNSW and IVFFlat; default PostgreSQL workspace is `default` [call-2c556838].

### 6.3 Version constraints / dependencies
**Partially supported.** Docker images reference PostgreSQL 18 (`pg18`): `gzdaniel/postgres-for-rag:pg18-age-pgvector` and `pgvector/pgvector:pg18` [call-f64c3f09]. One source states **no specific version constraints** are provided [call-c8463c9d]. No complete version matrix exists in the boundary.

---

## 7. Section 6 — Production storage architecture recommendation

> This recommendation is **reasoned from the evidence**, not an official LightRAG publication. It is labeled provisional because Neon/AGE compatibility and full backend compatibility were not verified.

### Recommended architecture (single-backend, simplest production path)

| Role | Backend | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| KV | `PGKVStorage` | PostgreSQL serves all four roles; official production recommendation [call-918fd425] [call-c21ffffd]. |
| Vector | `PGVectorStorage` (pgvector, HNSW or IVFFlat) | Avoids operating a separate vector DB; index type tunable via env vars [call-2c556838]. |
| Graph | `PGGraphStorage` (PostgreSQL + Apache AGE + pgvector) | Required extension stack; official Docker image `gzdaniel/postgres-for-rag:pg18-age-pgvector` bundles it [call-f64c3f09]. |
| Doc status | `PGDocStatusStorage` | Same PostgreSQL instance [call-3002da7b]. |

**Deployment:** Run PostgreSQL with pgvector and Apache AGE preloaded (e.g., the referenced Docker image or equivalent managed PostgreSQL where AGE can be installed). Configure via the environment variables in Section 6.2. Do **not** use the default in-memory/Json/Nano/NetworkX stores in production [call-c21ffffd] [call-7876a2cc].

### Neon-specific guidance
Neon is **not recommended as the sole production backend until Apache AGE support is confirmed**, because `PGGraphStorage` depends on AGE. If Neon is desired for KV/vector/doc-status (it supports PostgreSQL and `pg_embedding`), pair it with a separate graph backend (Neo4j or Memgraph) — but note the mixed-stack issue in GitHub issue #860 [call-b75d434f], which suggests testing a combined stack thoroughly or avoiding it.

### Alternative (specialized) architecture
If vector or graph workloads are large/specialized: PostgreSQL for KV + doc status; Milvus or Qdrant for vector; Neo4j or Memgraph for graph [call-c21ffffd] [call-7876a2cc]. This increases operational complexity and is only justified when single-backend PostgreSQL is insufficient.

### Key configuration cautions
